correctness.rationale: Write f(x)=h(x²), h(t)=(t+1)t²Q(t+t⁻¹), with Q(u)=u²+(a-1)u+(b-a-1). Because h(0)=1, the only failures are repeated Q roots, ramification at t=±1, or overlap with t=-1. In characteristic 3, Q(2)=a+b+1, Q(-2)=b-1, and disc(Q)=a²-a+2-b. A repeated root lowers the genus of the double-cover normalization from four. The two displayed involutions generate a group of order eight: the square of their product is the hyperelliptic involution. On the indicated basis, the coefficient matrix consists of two 2-by-2 blocks after grouping odd and even indices; both block determinants are a(b-1). At a=0 there are two rank-one blocks, each product of its Frobenius twists retaining rank one iff b is nonzero; at b=0 both blocks square to zero. This establishes the stable ranks and a-numbers, not just ordinary matrix ranks. For rank two, a slope other than 1/2 among the four residual slopes would require denominator at least three and its complementary slope, together at least six slopes. For the origin, independently of the Hermitian argument, on F_81 the image of the tenth-power map on nonzero elements is F_9^× and each fiber has ten elements. All nonzero F_9 elements are squares in F_81, so there are ten x values with x^10+1=0, two y values at every other x, and two points at infinity. Thus #C(F_81)=154, the maximal count, giving all Frobenius eigenvalues -9 and all slopes 1/2. The forbidden b values 1,-a-1,a²-a+2 coincide pairwise only at a=1,-1,0 respectively (in the order pairs 1–2, 1–3, 2–3); no triple collision occurs. Removing the two forbidden b at a=0 and separating the origin yields all of the marked counts, including an empty rank-two row over F_3.
residual_risks: The recorded enumerations are corroboration in four fields only; the discriminant and twist calculation, exact origin count, and forbidden-value census establish the universal result. No full automorphism group or moduli census is asserted.

value.rationale: The known dihedral locus has a simple but non-generic characteristic-three behavior: ordinary away from a line, rank two on its smooth nonzero part and supersingular but not superspecial at the origin. Identifying all three Newton strata and where they occur, including the disappearance of the rank-two stratum over the prime field, gives a usable complete classification for this standard normal form, beyond recomputing individual Cartier ranks.
residual_risks: Value is for this characteristic and marked family, not a genus-four moduli classification.
